memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses, "Say to the Israelites: 'On the fifteenth day
of the seventh month the LORD's Festival of Tabernacles begins, and it
lasts for seven days. The first day is a sacred assembly; do no regular
work'" - Lev 23:33-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The final festival of the year had families leaving their solid homes
to live in temporary shelters for a week. Branches and leaves overhead.
Thin walls. You could see the sky through the roof.

Why? To remember the wilderness years, when Israel had no permanent
address and depended on God for everything - manna each morning, water
from rock, a pillar of cloud to guide them.

It is easy to forget dependence once you own a house and have a full
barn. So once a year, God moved His people outdoors to remind them.

Dear friend, security has a way of making us forgetful. When
everything is arranged and provided for, prayer can become polite
rather than desperate.

The New Testament says believers are foreigners and strangers on earth
(Heb 11:13; 1 Pet 2:11). John writes that the Word became flesh and
made his dwelling among us - literally, He tabernacled among us (John
1:14). Jesus stepped into our temporary world.

And Paul reminds us that our earthly tent will be replaced by an
eternal house in heaven (2 Cor 5:1).

Hold this world a little more loosely today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Has comfort made me less dependent on God?
2. Am I holding my possessions and plans too tightly?
3. What would it look like to live as a citizen of heaven this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that this world is not my final home. Loosen my grip
on temporary things and fix my heart on what lasts. Amen.
